# Test index {#sec-appc}

### Summary

Use this appendix to find the exact name of a test before selecting it with CTest.
A row means that CMake registered a command for the recorded configuration; it does
not mean that the command ran or passed. The inventory separates snapy's commands
from tests belonging to fetched libraries, so a dependency's large test suite cannot
be mistaken for evidence about snapy's numerical methods.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Find snapy's registered test commands; the count is partitioned in @eq-appc-partition.

**Data.** In: configured CTest registrations; out: names, labels, defining calls and selected properties; counts are dimensionless integers.

**Placement.** Configure-time inventory, outside the solver's time-stepping loop.

**Activation.** This inventory uses `BUILD_TESTS=ON`, `CUDA=OFF`, `FULL_TESTS=OFF`, `NETCDF=ON`, `UCX=ON`; see the table header for the complete recorded switches.

**Guarantee / limits.** Exact registration counts for this CPU configuration; a CUDA build registers additional commands; no runtime, accuracy or coverage guarantee.

**Evidence.** The Tests layer below gives checks [C1]–[C4] and the limits of their evidence.
:::

**Local symbols.** $R$ is the set of all registered command names; $S$ is the
subset attributed to snapy and $D$ the subset attributed to dependencies.
$N_R$, $N_S$ and $N_D$ are their cardinalities (numbers of names). A CTest command
can run several assertions, so these counts are not counts of assertions or
independent physical cases.

### Derivation

The counting rule follows the registration backtrace, not a guess based on the
command's name. The following steps explain why the total in the generated table
can exceed its row count.

1. **Start with the configured registry.** CTest's `--show-only=json-v1` returns
   names and the CMake call stack that created each command. For example,
   `setup_test` ([`macro_setup_test.cmake:8-34`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/c0c38593d3d3f37bebe204a590610fd7daa05a5f/cmake/macros/macro_setup_test.cmake#L8-L34))
   ultimately calls `add_test`. A source file by itself is not a registration.
2. **Partition by origin.** The index generator assigns a command to $D$ if any
   backtrace frame is in the configured build's `_deps` directory; otherwise it
   assigns it to $S$. Every entry takes exactly one branch, giving
   $R=S\cup D$ and $S\cap D=\varnothing$. By inclusion–exclusion,
   $$
   N_R=N_S+N_D-|S\cap D|=N_S+N_D.
   $$ {#eq-appc-partition}
   This documents the index generator's classification, not a solver equation.
3. **Recover the displayed count.** Subtracting the dependency count gives
   $N_S=N_R-N_D$. The refresh at the code pin gives
   $1066-927=139$: 139 snapy rows and 927 Eigen registrations. These are
   configuration-specific measurements, not constants of snapy.[^appc-provenance]
4. **Keep count accuracy separate from solver accuracy.** Sorting names changes
   no membership and therefore no count. Python integer counts and SymPy integer
   arithmetic are exact here: the round-off error in the displayed subtraction is
   zero. There is no floating-point summation or truncation-order claim to make.
   The algebraic checks below verify the partition identity, its rearrangement and
   the numerical substitution separately.

### Numerical method

No numerical solver is executed to make this index. The generator walks each
registration backtrace, removes dependency entries, retains the outermost call
with a line number, then sorts snapy's rows by name. That call may be a helper or
a loop rather than a literal `add_test` containing the complete command name.
Labels are CTest selection metadata; an empty label cell means no recorded labels,
not an untested method. Likewise, a blank Notes cell means none of the properties
that this table displays, not that the command has no environment or timeout.

### Code

The table below links every registration to its defining call at
chengcli/snapy `c0c38593d3d3f37bebe204a590610fd7daa05a5f`. The C++ helper
`setup_test` appends the lower-case build type to the name, while
`snapy_add_python_test` ([`CMakeLists.txt:275-292`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/c0c38593d3d3f37bebe204a590610fd7daa05a5f/tests/CMakeLists.txt#L275-L292))
appends `_python`. A parallel helper invokes `torchrun`; the absence of a
`PROCESSORS` note does not prove that a command uses only one process:
`setup_parallel_test` ([`macro_setup_parallel_test.cmake:1-34`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/c0c38593d3d3f37bebe204a590610fd7daa05a5f/cmake/macros/macro_setup_parallel_test.cmake#L1-L34)).

**How to use this index.** Copy the full name, including its suffix, and first
check that it exists in your own configured build. For example, from the build
directory:

```bash
ctest -N -R '^test_eos[.]release$'
ctest --output-on-failure -R '^test_eos[.]release$'
ctest --show-only=json-v1 > ctest-registration.json
```

The anchored expression selects that command only. Build the corresponding
binaries before the second command. Inspect the JSON command and environment
when reproducing a run: the compact table deliberately omits machine paths and
most execution properties. For Python tests, set `SNAPY_TEST_PYTHONPATH` when
configuring to the installation built from the intended source; otherwise CMake
warns that tests import the installed snapy and do not constrain the checkout:
`SNAPY_TEST_PYTHONPATH` ([`CMakeLists.txt:468-482`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/c0c38593d3d3f37bebe204a590610fd7daa05a5f/tests/CMakeLists.txt#L468-L482)).
A skipped command is not a pass. In particular, some entries use exit code 125
as their skip condition, shown in Notes.

### Tests

These checks test the inventory and its explanation, rather than the registered
physics tests. The tolerance is exact equality because the objects being checked
are integer counts, names and generated text.

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| [C1] CTest JSON and plain listing | Both listings contain the same 1066 distinct names; the reduced fixture has 139 snapy entries and 927 dependency entries | exact | Integer partition of one configured registry |
| [C2] `python tools/gen_test_index.py --check`, in the report directory (@sec-appa-refresh) | The committed fragment equals the generator output from the committed fixture | byte-for-byte | Deterministic generation contract |
| [C3] Registration citations | Each row's helper occurs at its cited line in the pinned source | exact | CMake backtrace from the clean checkout |
| [C4] SymPy snippet below | Inclusion–exclusion, rearrangement and measured count substitution agree | symbolic zero | Exact integer arithmetic, no floating-point tolerance |

: Inventory checks; [C1]–[C4] are report checks, not CTest command names. {#tbl-appc-checks}

[C1] checks registration only; executables were not built or run for this refresh.
[C2] prevents hand edits to the generated rows from silently diverging from their
fixture. [C3] checks the defining call, not the assertions inside a test. [C4]
checks every algebraic transformation in the Derivation layer; it cannot prove
that a numerical method passes its tests.[^appc-provenance]

Run the following with Python and SymPy to reproduce [C4]:

```python
import sympy as sp
ns, nd, overlap = sp.symbols("ns nd overlap", integer=True, nonnegative=True)
union = ns + nd - overlap
assert sp.simplify(union.subs(overlap, 0) - (ns + nd)) == 0
assert sp.simplify((ns + nd) - nd - ns) == 0
assert sp.Integer(1066) - sp.Integer(927) == sp.Integer(139)
assert sp.Integer(139) + sp.Integer(927) == sp.Integer(1066)
print("[C4] PASS: 4 exact identities")
```

### Limits

This is the CPU configuration's registration inventory, not evidence of CPU or
CUDA execution. CUDA-only registrations and other switch combinations require a
separate configure and listing; none were checked here. Dependency counts can
also change with the compiler and available dependencies. The table does not
record individual numerical tolerances: follow each test's assertions and the
chapter's Tests layer for those. For measured verification see @sec-ch15, and for
configuration combinations see @sec-ch12-matrix.

[^appc-provenance]: Inventory refreshed from a clean checkout of chengcli/snapy
    `c0c38593d3d3f37bebe204a590610fd7daa05a5f` with `cmake -S snapy-pin -B snapy-pin/build -G Ninja
    -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DNETCDF=ON -DPNETCDF=OFF` (configure only, no build), then
    `python3 tools/gen_test_index.py --refresh snapy-pin/build`; CMake/CTest 4.4.4, torch 2.10.0,
    kintera 2.6.4, commux found (so `UCX=ON`). Recorded switches: Release, `BUILD_TESTS=ON`,
    `BUILD_EXAMPLES=OFF`, `CUDA=OFF`, `FULL_TESTS=OFF`, `NETCDF=ON`, `UCX=ON`. The committed
    `tools/ctest-index.json` records the reduced registration data; the table
    fragment is its generated output. [C1] is `ctest --show-only=json-v1` (1066 entries, 1066
    distinct names) against `ctest -N` (`Total Tests: 1066`) in that build directory. [C1]–[C4]
    were run with Python 3.12.10 and SymPy 1.14.0. No solver test verdict is claimed.
